title: I like Indian films — the sentence that flips its subject

notes: **In a पसंद sentence, the subject is the thing that is liked.** *मुझे फ़िल्में पसंद **हैं*** — हैं is plural because **फ़िल्में** is plural, not because of me. Compare *मुझे चाय पसंद **है*** (one thing) and *मुझे गाने पसंद **हैं*** (plural). ⚠️ The most common mistake is using हूँ because "I" feels like the subject. It isn't — you're the receiver. (Think of "films are pleasing to me".)

**पसंद है for likes in general, पसंद आया for something specific.** *मुझे हिंदी फ़िल्में पसंद **हैं*** = I like Hindi films (in general). *मुझे यह फ़िल्म पसंद **आई*** = I liked that film (the one I saw yesterday). ⚠️ The second is always about a specific experience that has already happened, and it's in the past.

**अच्छा लगता है is for activities, not things.** *मुझे पढ़ना अच्छा लगता है* = I enjoy reading. *मुझे यहाँ अच्छा लगता है* = I like it here. The form follows the thing being talked about: *मुझे यह जगह अच्छी लगती है* (जगह is feminine). It's the natural partner of पसंद है — one for things, the other for activities and feelings.

**Verbs can be used as nouns just as they are, and they're masculine.** **पढ़ना** = "reading", **खाना बनाना** = "cooking", **घूमना** = "going out, traveling", **सोना** = "sleeping". That's why *खाना* means "to eat" **and** "food" — they're the same word. ⚠️ Because the form is masculine, the adjective is masculine too: *पढ़ना **अच्छा** लगता है*.

**चाहना is for wanting to do something, and the structure goes back to normal.** *मैं गाने सुनना चाहती हूँ* — a bare **मैं**, and the verb agrees with **me**. Compare *मुझे गाने पसंद हैं*, which uses को. ⚠️ Two different structures for two similar ideas; both often appear side by side in one conversation, so practice switching between them.

**पसंद करना exists, but don't overuse it.** *मैं यह पसंद करती हूँ* sounds like "I prefer this / I choose this", not "I like it". For the feeling of liking, almost always use **पसंद है** or **अच्छा लगता है**. ⚠️ This is a classic mistake for English speakers, since "I like" covers both.

**About Lata Mangeshkar — Priya isn't exaggerating.** She recorded film songs for more than seven decades, and hers was the singing voice of nearly every heroine in Indian films for generations. ⚠️ And here's serious study advice: **Hindi film songs are the best practice material for beginners**, because the lyrics are written to be understood all over India — simple vocabulary, short lines, lots of repetition. Look for the lyrics in Devanagari, not in Latin letters.

after: ⚠️ Note the pair **मुझे जाना है** and **मैं जाना चाहती हूँ**. The first means "I have to go" (or "I need to go"); the second, "I want to go". The difference is subtle but real, and the first is far more common for politely ending a conversation: *अच्छा, मुझे जाना है* — "okay, I have to go".

grammars.title: Hobbies and free time
after: ⚠️ **क्रिकेट is more than a sport in India.** Asking *आपको क्रिकेट पसंद है?* almost always opens a long conversation, and knowing a player's name or two will get you further than a hundred vocabulary words.

blocks.text: Questions about likes are the safest way to start a conversation with someone new — much safer than politics or religion, and much more interesting than the weather.

blocks.title: Answering at the right level
items: **बहुत पसंद है।** — I really like it.
**हाँ, ठीक-ठाक।** — Yes, it's okay. (polite without lying)
**बिलकुल पसंद नहीं।** — I don't like it at all. ⚠️ Quite strong; save it for things you really dislike.
**पहले पसंद नहीं था, अब है।** — I didn't like it before, now I do. A line hosts always love.

blocks.text: The question **आपको भारत कैसा लगा?** will come your way again and again, and the answer matters — not because there's a right answer, but because people genuinely want to know. A natural answer names one specific thing rather than general praise: *मुझे यहाँ के लोग बहुत अच्छे लगे* (I really like the people here), *खाना बहुत स्वादिष्ट है* (the food is delicious), *भीड़ थोड़ी ज़्यादा है, लेकिन मुझे मज़ा आ रहा है* (it's a bit too crowded, but I'm enjoying it). ⚠️ Mentioning one small complaint amid the praise actually makes your answer sound honest, and Indians will happily agree with it.
